section: Social Studies (Paper-2) · Ch46 — Ancient & Medieval India — Deep 2
subject: Social Studies
stem: The Chola dynasty of South India, known for its powerful navy and maritime trade with Southeast Asia, built its most famous temple, the Brihadeeswarar Temple, at:
explanation: The Brihadeeswarar Temple, built by Raja Raja Chola I, stands at Thanjavur and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site — a landmark of Chola architecture.

section: Social Studies (Paper-2) · Ch46 — Ancient & Medieval India — Deep 2
subject: Social Studies
stem: The Vijayanagara Empire, whose ruins lie at Hampi in present-day Karnataka, reached its peak under which famous ruler?
explanation: Krishnadevaraya (1509-1529) was the most celebrated ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire, presiding over its cultural and military peak — a great patron of Telugu literature himself, having authored 'Amuktamalyada'.
